title: Find the Largest Element in an Array
description: Read N integers and print the largest value. The first input value is N, followed by N integers.
input_format: First integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000), followed by N space-separated integers.

starter_code.Python:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))
largest = numbers[0]
for number in numbers[1:n]:
    if number > largest:
        largest = number
print(largest)

learning_content.title: Arrays and traversal
learning_content.intro: An array stores multiple values in indexed positions. Initialize the current maximum with the first element, then visit the remaining elements and update it when a larger value appears.
points: Read the N values and initialize largest from the first value.
Update largest whenever a bigger value is found.
learning_content.note: Each value is compared at most once; the algorithm stores only the current maximum.

quiz.question: Why should largest be initialized from the first array element instead of always starting at zero?

options.label: To handle arrays containing only negative numbers
options.feedback: A zero starting value would incorrectly exceed every negative element.

options.label: To make the array length equal to zero
options.feedback: Initialization does not change the array length.

options.label: To skip comparing all later elements
options.feedback: The remaining elements still need to be checked.

options.label: To sort the array automatically
options.feedback: Tracking a maximum does not reorder the array.

quiz.explanation: Starting from the first actual value works for positive, zero and negative-only arrays.
